relevance_reason: The paper describes a family with the homoplasmic MT-ND6 G14459A mutation and pediatric-onset dystonia with basal ganglia lucencies. This is the LDYT phenotype.

findings.statement: Gropman et al. (2004) reported a family with the G14459A mtDNA mutation and a broad range of clinical features. The proband was a 3-year-old girl with anarthria, dystonia, spasticity and mild encephalopathy. Brain MRI showed bilateral, symmetric basal ganglia lucencies, and she had cerebral and systemic lactic acidosis. Her maternal first cousin had a much milder phenotype: a new-onset limp and mild hemiparesis, with similar MRI findings.
quotes: The proband was a 3-year-old girl with anarthria, dystonia, spasticity, and mild encephalopathy. MRI of the brain demonstrated bilateral, symmetric basal ganglia lucencies associated with cerebral and systemic lactic acidosis.
Her maternal first cousin presented with a new onset limp and mild hemiparesis along with similar MRI findings with a much milder phenotype.

findings.statement: In a family with a broad range of clinical features, including a proband with pediatric-onset dystonia, Gropman et al. (2004) identified the homoplasmic G14459A mutation in the mtDNA ND6 gene (MT-ND6). The mutation changes a moderately conserved alanine to valine at residue 72 (ala72-to-val), within the most evolutionarily conserved region of ND6. Family members carrying the mutation included both asymptomatic and symptomatic individuals, who had variable clinical and laboratory features of mitochondrial disease.
quotes: The mutation changes a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at amino acid residue 72, which is within the most evolutionarily conserved region of the ND6 protein.
Additional investigation of the family members with the mutation has revealed both asymptomatic and symptomatic individuals with variable clinical and laboratory features of mitochondrial disease.
This study re-emphasizes the heterogeneous clinical manifestation of homoplasmic G14459A mtDNA mutation even within the same family

findings.statement: Gropman et al. (2004) noted that clinical expression of the homoplasmic G14459A mutation varies even within a single family. They suggested that this supports the hypothesis that nuclear genes may modify the clinical expression of mitochondrial disease.
quotes: supports the hypothesis that nuclear genes may play a role in modifying the clinical expression of mitochondrial disease

relevance_reason: Functional cybrid study assigning a complex I defect to the MT-ND6 m.14459G>A mutation that causes LHON and/or dystonia.

findings.statement: Jun et al. (1996) noted that a heteroplasmic G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 of the mtDNA-encoded ND6 gene, which changes a moderately conserved alanine to valine at position 72 (A72V), had been identified as the cause of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or pediatric-onset dystonia in 3 unrelated families.
quotes: A heteroplasmic G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459 within the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)-encoded NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) gene has been identified as the cause of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or pediatric-onset dystonia in three unrelated families.
This ND6 np 14459 mutation changes a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at amino acid position 72 of the ND6 protein.

variants.as_reported: np 14459 G-to-A, alanine to valine at position 72

findings.statement: Jun et al. (1996) found a 60% reduction (P < 0.005) of complex I-specific activity in submitochondrial particles from EBV-transformed lymphoblasts of patients with the ND6 14459 mutation compared with controls, with no differences in activity of complexes II plus III, III, and IV.
quotes: revealed a 60% reduction (P < 0.005) of complex I-specific activity in patient cell lines compared with controls, with no differences in enzymatic activity for complexes II plus III, III and IV.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: Using transmitochondrial cybrids made by fusing enucleated patient lymphoblasts to a mtDNA-deficient (rho-0) lymphoblastoid line, Jun et al. (1996) assigned the complex I defect to the 14459 mutation: mutant cybrids showed a 39% reduction (p < 0.02) in complex I-specific activity relative to wildtype cybrids, with normal activity of other complexes. Kinetic analysis showed reduced Vmax with unchanged Km, and activity was inhibited by increasing concentrations of decylubiquinol, suggesting the mutation may alter the coenzyme Q-binding site of complex I.
quotes: Cybrids harboring the np 14459 mutation exhibited a 39% reduction (p < 0.02) in complex I-specific activity relative to wild-type cybrid lines but normal activity for the other complexes.
Kinetic analysis of the np 14459 mutant complex I revealed that the Vmax of the enzyme was reduced while the Km remained the same as that of wild type.
These observations suggest that the np 14459 mutation may alter the coenzyme Q-binding site of complex I.

relevance_reason: Original description of a kindred with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia, with maternal inheritance suggesting mitochondrial disease.

findings.statement: Novotny et al. (1986) studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber disease, 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, and 1 had both disorders.
quotes: We studied a kindred in which 8 members had the neuroretinopathy of Leber's disease; 14 had a progressive, generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration; and 1 had both disorders.

findings.statement: Novotny et al. (1986) found that the mode of inheritance in the kindred with Leber disease and dystonia was compatible with maternal transmission, and suggested that the disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.
quotes: The mode of inheritance was compatible with maternal transmission.
This neurologic disorder may be a mitochondrial disease.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies the MT-ND6 14459G>A mutation in a family with maternally inherited LHON and dystonia, which is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Jun et al. (1994) studied a 5-generation Hispanic family in which members had maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions, or both.
quotes: A five-generation Hispanic family expressing maternally transmitted Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or early-onset dystonia associated with bilateral basal ganglia lesions was studied.

findings.statement: In a 5-generation Hispanic family with LHON and/or dystonia, Jun et al. (1994) sequenced more than 90% of the mtDNA from a severely affected child and identified a G-to-A transition at nucleotide 14459 of the ND6 gene, resulting in an ala72-to-val substitution at a moderately conserved residue. The child's mtDNA belonged to Native American haplogroup D. The variant was not found in 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs or in 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, or 99 African mtDNAs. Six maternal relatives in 3 generations carried the mutation; one female with LHON was heteroplasmic. The authors suggested that it was the disease-causing mutation.
quotes: One of these variants, a G-to-A transition at nucleotide pair (np) 14459, changed a moderately conserved alanine to a valine at NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6 (ND6) residue 72.
The np 14459 variant was not found in any of 38 Native American haplogroup D mtDNAs, nor was it detected in 108 Asian, 103 Caucasian, or 99 African mtDNAs.
Six maternal relatives in three generations were tested and were found to harbor the mutation, with one female affected with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy being heteroplasmic.

variants.as_reported: np 14459 G-to-A; alanine to valine at ND6 residue 72

relevance_reason: Reports a Japanese family with LHON and dystonia carrying the MT-ND6 G14459A mutation.

findings.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) described a Japanese family in which affected members had generalized dystonia, attributed to striatal degeneration, beginning in childhood, and optic neuropathy beginning later in life.
quotes: We investigated a Japanese family with generalized dystonia attributed to striatal degeneration, which occurred in childhood, and late-onset optic neuropathy.

findings.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) sequenced the entire mtDNA of the proband from a Japanese family with LHON and dystonia and found 42 nucleotide changes compared with the revised Cambridge Reference Sequence. These included the G14459A mutation in the ND6 gene (MT-ND6), which was absent from 200 healthy Japanese controls. The authors noted that this mutation had previously been suggested as the cause of LHON and/or dystonia in Hispanic, African American, and Caucasian families, and they reported this as the first Japanese family with LHON and dystonia in which an mtDNA mutation was found.
quotes: We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.

The nucleotide G14459A mutation occurs in NADH dehydrogenase subunit 6, and has been suggested previously as the disease-causing mutation in Hispanic, African-American and Caucasian families of Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) and/or dystonia.
To our knowledge, this is the first case of LHON with dystonia that revealed a mtDNA mutation in a Japanese family.

findings.statement: Watanabe et al. (2006) also found an A3203G change in the proband's mtDNA. This change was absent from 200 healthy Japanese controls, and the authors stated that its significance remained unknown.
quotes: We identified two A3203G and G14459A mutations, which were completely absent in a population of 200 healthy Japanese, by estimating the frequency of each nucleotide change.
The significance of the A3203G mutation remains unknown.

relevance_reason: Reports a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia, with mtDNA ND4 and ND6 mutations and a complex I deficiency.

findings.statement: De Vries et al. (1996) studied a large Dutch family with a rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) associated with hereditary spastic dystonia. Some family members had both the neurologic and ophthalmologic lesions, while others had only one type of abnormality.
quotes: A rare form of Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) that is associated with hereditary spastic dystonia has been studied in a large Dutch family.
Neuropathy and ophthalmological lesions were present together in some family members, whereas only one type of abnormality was found in others.

findings.statement: In a large Dutch family with LHON and hereditary spastic dystonia, De Vries et al. (1996) found no previously reported LHON mtDNA mutations. Sequencing of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes found a heteroplasmic 11696A-G transition in the ND4 gene, causing a val312-to-ile substitution.
quotes: mtDNA mutations previously reported in LHON were not present.
A heteroplasmic A-->G transition at nucleotide position 11696 in the ND4 gene resulted in the substitution of an isoleucine for valine at amino acid position 312.

findings.statement: In the same Dutch family, De Vries et al. (1996) also found a homoplasmic 14596T-A transition in the ND6 gene, causing an ile26-to-met substitution. Neither mutation had been reported before.
quotes: A second mutation, a homoplasmic T-->A transition at nucleotide position 14596 in the ND6 gene, resulted in the substitution of a methionine for the isoleucine at amino acid residue 26.
Sequence analysis of the protein-coding mitochondrial genes revealed two previously unreported mtDNA mutations.

findings.statement: De Vries et al. (1996) found a severe complex I deficiency in a muscle biopsy from the family. They said this linked the new mtDNA mutations to the rare, complex phenotype that includes Leber optic neuropathy.
quotes: Biochemical analysis of a muscle biopsy revealed a severe complex I deficiency, providing a link between these unique mtDNA mutations and this rare, complex phenotype including Leber optic neuropathy.

phenotypes.text: severe complex I deficiency in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

relevance_reason: Reports a Chinese family with LDYT caused by the MT-ND3 m.10197G>A mutation, the first ND3 mutation reported to cause LDYT.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2009) described a Chinese family with 18 patients affected by Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT), a disorder in which vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia occur in variable combinations.
quotes: In this paper, we describe a Chinese family with 18 LDYT patients.
Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and dystonia (LDYT) is a mitochondrial disorder associated with variable combinations of vision loss and progressive generalized dystonia.

findings.statement: In a Chinese family with LDYT, Wang et al. (2009) used resequencing microarray analysis of the entire mitochondrial genome and identified a m.10197G>A mutation in the MTND3 gene, which substituted threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 (Ala47Thr), on a haplogroup D4b background. Quantitative heteroplasmy analysis showed that the mutation was homoplasmic in leukocytes of all affected individuals on the maternal side. The authors stated that this was the first ND3 mutation reported to cause LDYT.
quotes: revealed a mutation (mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A)) substituting a threonine for a highly conserved alanine at codon 47 of MTND3 on the background of haplogroup D4b
Quantitative analysis of the heteroplasmy of the mutation revealed a homoplasmy in the leukocytes of all the affected individuals on the maternal side.
This is the first description of the ND3 mutation causing LDYT.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2009) noted that the m.10197G>A mutation in MTND3 had also been reported in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome. They suggested that the clinical spectrum of this mutation is much wider and includes both LDYT and Leigh syndrome.
quotes: The mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation has recently been described in French and Korean patients with Leigh syndrome.
These findings suggest that the clinical presentations associated with the mtND3*10197A (m.10197G>A) mutation (ND3) are much wider, encompassing those of LDYT and Leigh syndrome.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2009) noted that LDYT, an oxidative phosphorylation disorder, had previously been attributed to mutations in the mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 genes. Their finding of an ND3 mutation in LDYT therefore added a further causative gene.
quotes: LDYT is a unique oxidative phosphorylation disorder caused by mutations in mitochondrial ND6 or ND4 gene.

relevance_reason: Reports an MT-ND1 3697G>A mutation that causes LHON and spastic dystonia in the same family, directly relevant to LDYT.

findings.statement: In a patient with LHON who did not carry one of the 3 primary LHON mutations, Spruijt et al. (2007) screened the complete mitochondrial DNA and found a pathogenic 3697G>A mutation in the MT-ND1 gene. The mutation appeared to be associated with isolated complex I deficiency. The authors determined the heteroplasmy level, but the abstract does not give it. They concluded that the mutation caused both LHON and spastic dystonia in the same family.
quotes: The complete mitochondrial DNA was screened for mutations in a patient with LHON without 1 of these 3 primary mutations. The heteroplasmy level and biochemical consequence of the mutation were determined.
A pathogenic 3697G>A/ND1 mutation was detected and seemed associated with an isolated complex I deficiency.
The 3697G>A/ND1 mitochondrial DNA mutation causes the LHON and spastic dystonia phenotype in the same family.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

findings.statement: Spruijt et al. (2007) described a family in which LHON and spastic dystonia occurred together. They said the family's clinical features were similar to those of previously described families with LHON and dystonia caused by an ND6 mutation.
quotes: To report a novel mutation that is associated with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) within the same family affected by spastic dystonia.
This family has similar clinical characteristics as the previously described families with LHON and dystonia with an ND6 mutation.

findings.statement: Spruijt et al. (2007) noted that the 3697G>A MT-ND1 mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome. They suggested that other genetic factors may contribute to how the disease is expressed clinically.
quotes: This mutation can also cause MELAS syndrome (which encompasses mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke), and other genetic factors may contribute to the clinical expression.

relevance_reason: The paper describes two pedigrees with the MT-ND6 G14459A mutation. One patient had spasticity/dystonia with lesions in the putamen. The pedigrees show variable LHON and dystonia phenotypes.

findings.statement: Tarnopolsky et al. (2004) described 2 Caucasian pedigrees with maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) phenotypes that varied greatly from patient to patient. In one patient with spasticity/dystonia, the only abnormal screening test was a high T2 signal in both putamina. A male patient in the second pedigree had optic neuropathy without spasticity or dystonia.
quotes: The maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) phenotypes showed extreme clinical variability and the only screening test that was abnormal in the patient with spasticity/dystonia was a high T2 signal in the putamen bilaterally.
The male patient in the second pedigree showed features of optic neuropathy without spasticity/dystonia.

findings.statement: Tarnopolsky et al. (2004) found the mitochondrial DNA G14459A transition (14,459 G-to-A) in 2 Caucasian pedigrees with maternally inherited LHON, with or without spasticity/dystonia. They concluded that the findings further supported a causal role for this mutation in both LHON and spasticity/dystonia.
quotes: We describe the clinical features and molecular analysis of two Caucasian pedigrees with the 14,459 guanosine (G) --> adenine (A) transition.
These results further support that the 14,459 G --> A transition mutation is causally related to LHON and spasticity/dystonia.

findings.statement: Tarnopolsky et al. (2004) observed that the G14459A mutation produced very different phenotypes. In one pedigree, a patient had spasticity/dystonia with putaminal lesions. In the other pedigree, a male had optic neuropathy without spasticity or dystonia.
quotes: The maternally inherited Leber hereditary optic neuropathy (LHON) phenotypes showed extreme clinical variability

relevance_reason: The original clinical description of familial dystonia with visual failure and striatal lucencies (Marsden syndrome), which is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Marsden et al. (1986) described a disorder in 7 members of 2 families in whom dystonia was variably associated with subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy, and with striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen.
quotes: A unique disorder is described in seven members of two families in whom dystonia was variably associated with subacute visual loss or asymptomatic optic atrophy, and striking bilateral symmetrical lucencies on CT scan, especially involving the putamen.

phenotypes.text: bilateral symmetrical putaminal lucencies on CT

findings.statement: Marsden et al. (1986) suggested that the condition might be a variant of Leigh disease but noted considerable differences from pathologically proven Leigh disease, and stated that it must be excluded in all patients thought to have idiopathic dystonia, subacute visual failure similar to Leber optic neuropathy, or a combination of these disorders.
quotes: It is possible that this is a variant of Leigh's disease. However, there were considerable differences between these patients and those with pathologically proven Leigh's disease.
This condition must be excluded in all patients thought to have idiopathic dystonia, subacute visual failure similar to Leber's optic neuropathy, or a combination of these disorders.

relevance_reason: Only the title is available. It reports a new manifestation of Leber disease and a new explanation for its unusual inheritance, which fits the Leber optic atrophy and dystonia entry. No clinical details, patient numbers or genetic data are available.

findings.statement: Wallace (1970) described a new manifestation of Leber disease (Leber hereditary optic neuropathy) and proposed a new explanation for the agent responsible for its unusual pattern of inheritance.
quotes: A new manifestation of Leber's disease and a new explanation for the agency responsible for its unusual pattern of inheritance.

relevance_reason: Reports two additional pedigrees with the MTND6 T14459A mutation, confirming its association with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or dystonia.

findings.statement: Shoffner et al. (1995) described two more pedigrees carrying the MTND6*LDYT14459A mutation. In one pedigree, two family members developed Leber hereditary optic neuropathy, and the daughter had basal ganglia lesions that caused no symptoms. In the second pedigree, one person had generalized dystonia beginning in childhood, along with bilateral basal ganglia lesions.
quotes: Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy developed in two family members in one pedigree. The daughter had clinically silent basal ganglia lesions.
In a second pedigree, a single individual presented with childhood-onset generalized dystonia and bilateral basal ganglia lesions.

findings.statement: Shoffner et al. (1995) found the MTND6*LDYT14459A point mutation in the ND6 subunit of complex I, at mtDNA position 14459, in two pedigrees beyond the original family. The authors concluded that this confirmed the mutation's association with Leber hereditary optic neuropathy and/or dystonia. They called it the first genetic abnormality identified as a cause of generalized dystonia.
quotes: A novel point mutation in the ND6 subunit of complex I at position 14,459 of the mitochondrial DNA (MTND6*LDY T14459A) was identified as a candidate mutation for the highly tissue-specific disease.
These results confirm the association of the MTND6*LDYT14459A mutation with Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy and/or dystonia.

findings.statement: Shoffner et al. (1995) did not find the MTND6*LDYT14459A mutation in patient groups with Leigh disease, dystonia plus complex neurodegeneration, or Leber hereditary optic neuropathy. They suggested that the mutation is highly tissue-specific and therefore produces a narrow range of phenotypes.
quotes: Patient groups that included individuals with Leigh's disease, dystonia plus complex neurodegeneration, and Leber's hereditary optic neuropathy did not harbor the MTND6*LDYT14459A mutation, suggesting that this mutation displays a high degree of tissue specificity, thus producing a narrow phenotypic range.
